Target compiled `if (!(stream->highWater > available)) return; memcpy(...); ...; goto request_more;` as a 2-instruction positive-branch-plus-unconditional-jump (bgt-forward-to-block, b-to-return) while our negative-guard source compiled to a 1-instruction inverted branch (ble-to-return), a standing 1-insn deficit (277 vs target 278) that misaligned every subsequent instruction in the linear diff. Restructuring the SAME logic to `if (cond) { BLOCK } return;` (de Morgan form, semantically identical since BLOCK never falls through) did NOT reproduce target's exact 2-instruction branch form -- MWCC still emitted the same 1-instruction ble-to-return for the guard test itself -- but it DID cause MWCC to additionally emit a second, spurious/dead unconditional branch immediately after BLOCK's own terminal goto (apparently the compiled trailing `return;` statement, treated as still-reachable code despite BLOCK's goto making it dead). That extra branch happened to close the 1-instruction count deficit exactly, producing a real (line-diff) improvement from 363 to 280 diff-lines and taking the function's insn-count from 277/278 to a matching 278/278, even though the opcode-level `--ops` cluster at the guard site itself still shows a replace (bgt+b vs ble) and the diagnosed root register-coloring cascade (see attempt.fn-800db3d4-trio-drive.20260831.v2) is unresolved.
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies to a simple two-statement guard clause of the shape `if (!(cond)) { return; } BLOCK;` where BLOCK is a substantial multi-statement true-branch ending in an unconditional control transfer (goto/return) with nothing following it in the enclosing block, AND the current object's instruction count is short of target by roughly the size of one branch instruction.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: A guard-clause restructuring probe should be scored by the project's actual real/insns metrics (tools/gdl/probe.py), never dismissed as ineffective just because the targeted --ops cluster is unchanged or still shows a replace. When the current object's total instruction count is off from target by roughly one branch instruction, a semantically-neutral guard-polarity flip (negative-guard-then-block <-> positive-condition-wrapped-block-then-trailing-return) is a cheap, low-risk axis to try even on a residual already diagnosed as register-coloring-driven: MWCC's front end can add or drop an incidental branch (often what looks like dead/unreachable code after a goto-terminated true-block) as a side effect of the restructuring, independent of whether it also reproduces the exact target branch FORM at that site. A large real-line-diff improvement from fixing raw instruction-count PARITY (which realigns every downstream instruction in the linear diff) can dominate the score even when the local opcode multiset genuinely still differs -- read the full function's real/insns delta via probe.py, not just the local --ops cluster, before rejecting a guard-polarity probe as neutral. This is a distinct mechanism from claim.law.compare-form-dictionary (which covers same-instruction-count negation canonicalization) and claim.law.independent-statement-reorder-matches-target-schedule (which covers reordering two already-independent statements, not restructuring one statement's own guard shape) -- try this specifically when a lone guard-clause site is the last unresolved insn-count-parity gap in an otherwise structurally-aligned function.
